title: Bar: custom command widget shows raw JSON when output has an empty "text"
body:
**System:** Omarchy 4.0.4-1, NVIDIA RTX 3090, Hyprland (Lua config)

**What happens**
A custom `"type": "command"` bar widget whose script prints Waybar-style JSON with an empty text field, e.g.

```json
{"text":"","class":"ok"}
```

shows that whole JSON line as its label in the bar instead of hiding or showing nothing.

**Expected**
An empty `"text"` should render an empty (hidden) widget, the same as Waybar. The README says the command "may print plain text or Waybar-style JSON", and an empty text is the usual Waybar way to hide a module.

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Add to `~/.config/omarchy/shell.json` under `bar.layout.right`:
   `{ "id": "test-empty", "type": "command", "exec": "echo '{\"text\":\"\",\"class\":\"ok\"}'", "interval": 5 }`
2. The bar shows `{"text":"","class":"ok"}`.

**Cause**
`CustomCommandModule.update()` in `shell/plugins/bar/Bar.qml`:

```js
outputText = data.text || String(raw || "").trim()
```

An empty string is falsy, so the fallback to the raw output kicks in even though the JSON parsed fine. A possible fix is to fall back only when the output wasn't JSON, e.g. check `data.text !== undefined` (or whether `Util.parseModuleJson` succeeded) before using `raw`.

**Workaround**
Print nothing at all instead of JSON with an empty text.
